headline: Simulation and graph learning map conformational routes in proteins and complexes
label: Computational Molecular Systems Modeling
summary: Recent preprints and one publication pair MD, Markov models, and learned restraints to link protein dynamics with function and disease mutations.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of conformational ensembles, rather than single static structures, to explain function. Molecular dynamics underlies most of these studies: GaMD with Shape-GMM and LDA shows that L405D in SARS-CoV-2 nsp13 decouples ATP hydrolysis from RNA translocation, and multimicrosecond MD of liver pyruvate kinase tracks how alanine rewires FBP-activated communication pathways. Markov state models and forward-flux sampling define ligand binding paths on disordered peptides and folding flux pathways, while an ensemble-allosteric framework reconciles gain- and loss-of-function IP3R1 disease mutations. Newer elements include AIMS-Fold, which steers diffusion-based co-folding with XL-MS and HDX-MS restraints, and GISTnet-MD, an explainable graph neural network for residue-level binding signatures. AlloDyn adds ensemble dynamics to allosteric site prediction and flags benchmark leakage.
